newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht quoted at new record low against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht quoted at new record low against dollar.

text.p: The Thai baht was quoted on Wednesday at a new record low of 32.15/32.50 against the dollar as players sought refuge in the greenback, dealers said.

Some foreign and local banks onshore were quoting the baht at new lows to test the resolve of the Bank of Thailand and see if it would intervene in the market to stabilise the sliding currency, they added. "There is so far no sign of any central bank intervention," a dealer with a local bank told Reuters.
In the offshore market, the baht was quoted higher at 31.20/31.40 to the dollar.

The Thai central bank said on July 2, after it freed the baht from its peg to a trade-weighted basket of currencies dominated by the dollar and allowed it into a managed float, that it would intervene if the baht fell to an "appropriate level".
When the baht hit around 30 to the dollar last week, a top central bank official said it had fallen low enough.
Earlier on Wednesday, the baht fell to its previous record low of 31.60 on talk that commercial demand for dollars had dampened baht sentiment in a thin market.
Central bank officials declined to comment on any plans to intervene to prop the baht up.
But one official said the baht's drop was exaggerated because of the thinness of trade in the market.

Thanasak Chantarovat, deputy director of the central bank's banking department, told reporters that the baht slide on Wednesday was aggravated by poor first-half earnings of commercial banks and finance companies.
He said the weak bank earnings stemmed from their required higher reserves for doubtful loans but he added that the increased provisions would strengthen banks in the long run.
The official said sentiment on the baht could also be hurt by expectations that data on the level of non-performing loans of financial institutions would be released soon to the stock market.
"They could have negative psychological effect if the figures are high but I don't think they would be that bad," he said.
